independently — formulating hypotheses, testing conjectures computationally, building proof sketches, and pivoting when approaches fail, rather than passively summarizing existing research.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003ePython Math Sandbox\u003c/strong\u003e: A dedicated computational tool gives the agent a full mathematical laboratory with SymPy (symbolic algebra/calculus), NumPy (numerical computation), SciPy (optimization, integration, special functions), and Matplotlib — enabling it to run experiments, verify proofs numerically, and search for counterexamples.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eSymbolic Calculator\u003c/strong\u003e: A lightweight tool for quick symbolic operations (simplify, factor, solve, integrate, differentiate, series expansion) without writing full Python scripts.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eDeep Search Agent\u003c/strong\u003e: Uses LangGraph's deep-search workflow (with a ReAct fallback) to supplement its own thinking with web research — looking up specific theorems, checking whether an approach has been tried, or finding relevant papers.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eTuned for Creativity\u003c/strong\u003e: Higher LLM temperature (configurable via \u003ccode\u003eAIOPS_LLM_TEMPERATURE\u003c/code\u003e) encourages novel and diverse mathematical thinking across iterations.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003ePersistent Research Memory\u003c/strong\u003e: Stores every daily update, plus structured summaries, next steps, and citations in Azure Table Storage.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eResume \u0026amp; Continue\u003c/strong\u003e: On each run, the agent ingests the historical context and advances the same problem instead of starting from scratch.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eInfinite Timeline UI\u003c/strong\u003e: A Flask route (\u003ccode\u003e/ai-open-problem-solver\u003c/code\u003e) serves an infinite-scroll page that streams the latest findings first and lazily loads earlier milestones from storage.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eDynamic Problem Picker\u003c/strong\u003e: The UI queries Azure Table Storage to populate a dropdown of all tracked problems, so you can switch research threads instantly.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eProblem Catalog Table\u003c/strong\u003e: Configure \u003ccode\u003eaiops_problem_table_name\u003c/code\u003e for the virtual world. Using Azure OpenAI and a structured prompt-response loop, the system generates daily high-level decisions on critical areas such as economy, society, environment, and global politics. Each decision is designed to be realistic, impactful, and ethically informed, balancing immediate outcomes with long-term sustainability. The goal is to create an engaging and evolving narrative that demonstrates the capabilities of generative AI while inviting users to reflect on governance and the complexities of decision-making in a simulated world. \u003ca href=\"https://medium.com/@abozar-alizadeh/giving-the-ai-government-a-face-and-a-voice-building-genboxs-self-producing-newsroom-db7f57b9e1c7\" rel=\"nofollow\"\u003eRead more\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eGrounded in the real world:\u003c/strong\u003e each decision is built in two phases. First the AI \u003cstrong\u003epicks a fresh topic\u003c/strong\u003e for the day (diversified away from recent ones). Once the topic is set — but \u003cem\u003ebefore\u003c/em\u003e writing the decision — GenBox runs an internet research step using the model's \u003cstrong\u003enative web search\u003c/strong\u003e (the Azure OpenAI Responses API \u003ccode\u003eweb_search\u003c/code\u003e tool, the same approach AIBlog and ComicBook use), gathering the current real-world \u003cstrong\u003eachievements, challenges, blockers, and limits\u003c/strong\u003e on that topic. That briefing is fed into the second phase, so the AI's decision proposes concrete, actionable solutions to \u003cem\u003ereal\u003c/em\u003e current problems rather than abstract policy; the chosen topic and the source URLs it grounded on are saved alongside the decision. The research is best-effort: if web search is unavailable, the decision is still produced (just ungrounded).\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe decisions are presented on a retro CRT television: the classic experience scrolls the day's decision as green terminal text, and the four physical knobs let you step backward/forward through the timeline and pause or reverse the scroll.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e📐 \u003cstrong\u003eArchitecture:\u003c/strong\u003e \u003ca href=\"/abozaralizadeh/SandBox/blob/main/GenBox/architecture.md\"\u003eTechnical flow and Instead of reading the (often long) decision verbatim, it's covered like a real bulletin — a short anchor headline (\"The AI Government today decided to…\"), a field report with b-roll, and a brief interview — all with natively generated speech and lip-sync from \u003cstrong\u003eSora 2 on Azure OpenAI\u003c/strong\u003e. When a video is available it becomes the default display mode; the original scrolling text is always one button-press away.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch4 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eKey Features\u003c/h4\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-key-features-2\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Key Features\" href=\"#key-features-2\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eNews-Bulletin Format\u003c/strong\u003e: An \u003cstrong\u003eOpenAI Agents SDK\u003c/strong\u003e \"Producer\" agent distills the decision (not a verbatim read) into a segmented shot list — \u003cstrong\u003eanchor lead → field report → interview → sign-off\u003c/strong\u003e — with every spoken line sized to Sora's 4/8/12-second clip limits.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eAnchor, Reporter \u0026amp; Interviewee\u003c/strong\u003e: Beyond the studio anchor, the segment features an on-location \u003cstrong\u003ecorrespondent\u003c/strong\u003e and an \u003cstrong\u003einterviewee\u003c/strong\u003e (an official, expert, or citizen), each rendered as their own on-camera speaker.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eNative Speech \u0026amp; B-Roll\u003c/strong\u003e: Sora 2 generates synchronized audio and dialogue directly, so each speaker actually talks. The producer interleaves face-free b-roll cutaways (cityscapes, factories, solar farms, maps) to illustrate the report.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eScene Consistency (via remix)\u003c/strong\u003e: Sora 2 has no seed and rejects human faces in \u003ccode\u003einput_reference\u003c/code\u003e, so each speaker's \u003cem\u003efirst\u003c/em\u003e clip is a fresh generation and every later clip of that same speaker is a \u003cstrong\u003eremix\u003c/strong\u003e of it — reusing the source's layout, wardrobe, and lighting so the anchor/reporter/interviewee stay recognizable. Face-free b-roll is additionally chained via last-frame→first-frame (\u003ccode\u003einput_reference\u003c/code\u003e).\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eSeamless Stitching\u003c/strong\u003e: All clips are merged with a bundled static \u003ccode\u003effmpeg\u003c/code\u003e (via \u003ccode\u003eimageio-ffmpeg\u003c/code\u003e, no system package required) into a single MP4 stored in Azure Blob Storage and streamed back to the TV.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eNon-Blocking Generation\u003c/strong\u003e: Both the decision text (topic + web research + write) and the video/narration run in background threads guarded by single-flight table locks, so the page never hangs. While today's bulletin is still being prepared the TV shows \u003cstrong\u003eno-signal static\u003c/strong\u003e (\"Tuning in…\") and re-polls \u003ccode\u003e/get-string\u003c/code\u003e until the text is ready; it then switches to video automatically once the segment is ready. Status is polled via \u003ccode\u003e/genbox-video-status\u003c/code\u003e and cached per day.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eCRT Controls, Now for Video\u003c/strong\u003e: The \u003cstrong\u003elowest knob\u003c/strong\u003e toggles between the classic scrolling text and the news video. The back/next knobs move through the timeline (loading each day's video when available), and the pause knob pauses/plays the clip. The narration renders quickly — well before the video — and plays over the scrolling text, with the scroll slowed to match the speech length. It's gated, cached, stored (in the video blob container), and referenced in the table just like the video, and served same-origin via \u003ccode\u003e/genbox-audio\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eMultiple Sora resources / distributed credits.\u003c/strong\u003e Sora's API is job-scoped: a \u003ccode\u003ecreate\u003c/code\u003e call returns a video id that only exists on the resource that served it, so the follow-up \u003ccode\u003epoll {id}\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003edownload {id}\u003c/code\u003e must hit that \u003cem\u003esame\u003c/em\u003e resource — a round-robin gateway in front of several resources breaks this affinity. <p dir="auto">These projects are not isolated tools but rather facets of a broader exploration into AI autonomy. The presence of these three distinct yet related projects reveals a cohesive vision. My work is not merely about code but about exploring the potential of agentic AI to interact with and reason about the real world in increasingly sophisticated ways. The repository's associated topics, such as AI governance, ethics, and simulation, underscore this focus on the higher-order implications of autonomous systems.</p>

<p dir="auto">Multi-Agent AI Comic Strip Generator<br>
ComicBook produces a daily AI-generated comic strip on the <strong>OpenAI Agents SDK</strong>, orchestrated as a <strong>handoff chain</strong>: Director → Storyteller → Cartoonist → Reteller. A single <code>Runner.run(Director)</code> drives the whole episode; each agent calls its <code>transfer_to_<next></code> tool to pass control on, and a <strong>deterministic recovery</strong> runs any stage a missed handoff skipped — so a comic always ships. The Director also consults an <strong>OriginalityCritic</strong> sub-agent (via <code>as_tool</code>) before starting a new arc.
<a href="https://medium.com/towards-artificial-intelligence/the-comic-that-draws-itself-building-a-daily-ai-graphic-novel-studio-da4f7a61e39c" rel="nofollow">Read more</a></p>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h4 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Agent Pipeline</h4><a id="user-content-agent-pipeline" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Agent Pipeline" href="#agent-pipeline"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>Director</strong> (temp 1.2) — Invents original story arcs. For a new arc it <strong>web-searches for fresh inspiration</strong>, forms a candidate, calls <code>check_arc_originality</code>, and retries until it's distinct from recent arcs; decides arc length organically; writes the story outline; plans each episode's panels and tone. Then hands off to the Storyteller.</li>
<li><strong>OriginalityCritic</strong> (temp 0.2, <code>as_tool</code>) — Reads recent arcs and judges a candidate's core story (plot shape, conflict, archetypes, setting, art style), returning <code>ok</code> / <code>too_similar</code> + retry guidance. <code>start_new_arc</code> additionally refuses a recently-used art style.</li>
<li><strong>Storyteller</strong> (temp 0.5) — Transforms the Director's plan into a panel-by-panel script (dialogue, captions, SFX, camera angles, per-panel size), then hands off to the Cartoonist.</li>
<li><strong>Cartoonist</strong> — Pulls the full arc roster, generates a <strong>character reference sheet</strong> for visual consistency, then draws each panel sequentially using the reference via Azure OpenAI image editing, assembles the English HTML page, and hands off to the Reteller.</li>
<li><strong>Reteller</strong> (temp 0.9) — In one run, <strong>retells</strong> the episode natively in Italian and Persian over the same fixed images (not a translation), adapting + saving the localized outline on episode 1 and maintaining a per-language glossary.</li>
</ul>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h4 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Key Features</h4><a id="user-content-key-features" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Key Features" href="#key-features"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>Dynamic Story Arcs</strong>: arcs run for as many episodes as they need (3, 8, 15…), then close and a completely fresh arc begins. A <strong>three-layer originality guard</strong> (prompt-mandated search + the OriginalityCritic + an art-style refusal) keeps each arc genuinely different.</li>
<li><strong>Character Consistency</strong>: one character reference sheet per arc (cached), then every panel is drawn sequentially with that reference (plus mid-arc key panels and prior-episode anchors).</li>
<li><strong>Multi-language editions</strong>: English is native; the Reteller produces it/fa over the shared art. The <strong>main title comes from the arc</strong> (consistent every episode) with the episode's native title shown as a <strong>subtitle</strong>.</li>
<li><strong>Readability guard</strong>: the page's color theme is contrast-checked at render time — any low-contrast text is auto-flipped to near-black/near-white, so a box is never light-on-light or dark-on-dark.</li>
<li><strong>Local debug mode</strong>: <code>DEBUG=true</code> isolates all reads/writes to a separate <code>arc_debug</code> partition (and lock) so local tests never touch production; <code>DEBUG_SAVE=false</code> is a pure dry run.</li>
<li><strong>Arc Memory</strong>: Azure Table Storage tracks arc metadata, outlines, glossaries, key panels, and episode summaries so each strip honors continuity.</li>
<li><strong>Responsive Comic Layout</strong>: comic-book styling (speech bubbles, caption boxes, SFX) that adapts to mobile and desktop.</li>
<li><strong>Frontend</strong>: <code>/comicbook</code> fetches the latest strip (or a selected date) and renders the comic page.</li>
</ul>

<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>OpenAI Agents SDK</strong> (<code>openai-agents</code>) — agent definitions, <code>@function_tool</code> tools (deterministic only), <strong>handoffs</strong> with <code>input_filter</code> + <code>prompt_with_handoff_instructions</code>, sub-agents via <code>Agent.as_tool</code>, <code>Runner.run()</code></li>
<li><strong>Azure OpenAI</strong> — chat model (configurable, e.g. <code>gpt-5.4</code>) for the agents, <code>gpt-image</code> for image generation (1-hour client timeouts, override via <code>COMICBOOK_LLM_TIMEOUT</code> / <code>COMICBOOK_IMAGE_TIMEOUT</code>)</li>
<li><strong>Azure Table & Blob Storage</strong> — arc/episode persistence (with <code>DEBUG</code> partition isolation), image and HTML hosting</li>
</ul>

<p dir="auto">Autonomous Creative Mathematician & Deep-Research Agent<br>
AI Open Problem Solver extends the LangGraph infrastructure with a creative autonomous mathematician that actively attempts to solve open mathematical problems — including the Millennium Prize Problems. Rather than just searching the internet for existing work, the agent formulates original conjectures, runs computational experiments, develops proof strategies, and uses web research only as a supplement. Each daily iteration is recorded as a rich HTML lab notebook entry. <a href="https://pub.towardsai.net/can-my-autonomous-ai-agent-solve-a-millennium-problem-and-win-1-000-000-3ff8fff8a786" rel="nofollow">Read more</a></p>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h4 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Key Capabilities</h4><a id="user-content-key-capabilities" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Key Capabilities" href="#key-capabilities"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>Creative Problem Solving</strong>: The agent thinks independently — formulating hypotheses, testing conjectures computationally, building proof sketches, and pivoting when approaches fail, rather than passively summarizing existing research.</li>
<li><strong>Python Math Sandbox</strong>: A dedicated computational tool gives the agent a full mathematical laboratory with SymPy (symbolic algebra/calculus), NumPy (numerical computation), SciPy (optimization, integration, special functions), and Matplotlib — enabling it to run experiments, verify proofs numerically, and search for counterexamples.</li>
<li><strong>Symbolic Calculator</strong>: A lightweight tool for quick symbolic operations (simplify, factor, solve, integrate, differentiate, series expansion) without writing full Python scripts.</li>
<li><strong>Deep Search Agent</strong>: Uses LangGraph's deep-search workflow (with a ReAct fallback) to supplement its own thinking with web research — looking up specific theorems, checking whether an approach has been tried, or finding relevant papers.</li>
<li><strong>Tuned for Creativity</strong>: Higher LLM temperature (configurable via <code>AIOPS_LLM_TEMPERATURE</code>) encourages novel and diverse mathematical thinking across iterations.</li>
<li><strong>Persistent Research Memory</strong>: Stores every daily update, plus structured summaries, next steps, and citations in Azure Table Storage.</li>
<li><strong>Resume & Continue</strong>: On each run, the agent ingests the historical context and advances the same problem instead of starting from scratch.</li>
<li><strong>Infinite Timeline UI</strong>: A Flask route (<code>/ai-open-problem-solver</code>) serves an infinite-scroll page that streams the latest findings first and lazily loads earlier milestones from storage.</li>
<li><strong>Dynamic Problem Picker</strong>: The UI queries Azure Table Storage to populate a dropdown of all tracked problems, so you can switch research threads instantly.</li>
<li><strong>Problem Catalog Table</strong>: Configure <code>aiops_problem_table_name</code> for the dedicated problem registry table; add or remove problems there to control which threads are available in the UI.</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">Set up the storage names (<code>aiops_table_name</code>, <code>aiops_blob_name</code>) and optionally define <code>AIOPS_DEFAULT_PROBLEM</code> in <code>.env</code> to choose the default unsolved problem tackled by the agent. Tune creativity with <code>AIOPS_LLM_TEMPERATURE</code> (default <code>0.8</code>) and sandbox execution time with <code>AIOPS_SANDBOX_TIMEOUT</code> (default <code>120</code> seconds).</p>

<p dir="auto">LangGraph is the backbone of this project, providing a stateful, multi-actor environment for building agent workflows. Key features of LangGraph include:</p>
<ul dir="auto">

<li><strong>Persistence</strong>: Saves the state of the application after each step, supporting error recovery and human-in-the-loop workflows.</li>
<li><strong>Human-in-the-Loop</strong>: Enables interruption of graph execution for human approval or edits.</li>
<li><strong>Streaming Support</strong>: Outputs are streamed as they are generated by each node.</li>
<li><strong>Integration with LangChain</strong>: Seamlessly integrates with LangChain and LangSmith for enhanced functionality.</li>
</ul>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">GenBox</h2><a id="user-content-genbox" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: GenBox" href="#genbox"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">This experimental project explores the potential of AI as an autonomous decision-maker for a virtual world. Using Azure OpenAI and a structured prompt-response loop, the system generates daily high-level decisions on critical areas such as economy, society, environment, and global politics. Each decision is designed to be realistic, impactful, and ethically informed, balancing immediate outcomes with long-term sustainability. The goal is to create an engaging and evolving narrative that demonstrates the capabilities of generative AI while inviting users to reflect on governance and the complexities of decision-making in a simulated world. <a href="https://medium.com/@abozar-alizadeh/giving-the-ai-government-a-face-and-a-voice-building-genboxs-self-producing-newsroom-db7f57b9e1c7" rel="nofollow">Read more</a></p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Grounded in the real world:</strong> each decision is built in two phases. First the AI <strong>picks a fresh topic</strong> for the day (diversified away from recent ones). Once the topic is set — but <em>before</em> writing the decision — GenBox runs an internet research step using the model's <strong>native web search</strong> (the Azure OpenAI Responses API <code>web_search</code> tool, the same approach AIBlog and ComicBook use), gathering the current real-world <strong>achievements, challenges, blockers, and limits</strong> on that topic. That briefing is fed into the second phase, so the AI's decision proposes concrete, actionable solutions to <em>real</em> current problems rather than abstract policy; the chosen topic and the source URLs it grounded on are saved alongside the decision. The research is best-effort: if web search is unavailable, the decision is still produced (just ungrounded).</p>
<p dir="auto">The decisions are presented on a retro CRT television: the classic experience scrolls the day's decision as green terminal text, and the four physical knobs let you step backward/forward through the timeline and pause or reverse the scroll.</p>

<p dir="auto">I invite you to explore the very simple interface at <a href="https://SandBoxes.Live/genbox" rel="nofollow">https://SandBoxes.Live/genbox</a>, where you can witness the AI’s daily decisions and follow the evolving narrative of this virtual world.</p>
<p dir="auto"><a target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" href="https://github.com/abozaralizadeh/SandBox/blob/main/static/sample.png?raw=true"><img src="https://github.com/abozaralizadeh/SandBox/raw/main/static/sample.png?raw=true" alt="TV" style="max-width: 100%;"></a></p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">AI News Anchor (Sora 2 Video)</h3><a id="user-content-ai-news-anchor-sora-2-video" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: AI News Anchor (Sora 2 Video)" href="#ai-news-anchor-sora-2-video"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">GenBox now broadcasts each daily decision as an AI-generated <strong>TV news segment</strong> that plays on the CRT in place of the scrolling text. Instead of reading the (often long) decision verbatim, it's covered like a real bulletin — a short anchor headline ("The AI Government today decided to…"), a field report with b-roll, and a brief interview — all with natively generated speech and lip-sync from <strong>Sora 2 on Azure OpenAI</strong>. When a video is available it becomes the default display mode; the original scrolling text is always one button-press away.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h4 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Key Features</h4><a id="user-content-key-features-2" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Key Features" href="#key-features-2"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>News-Bulletin Format</strong>: An <strong>OpenAI Agents SDK</strong> "Producer" agent distills the decision (not a verbatim read) into a segmented shot list — <strong>anchor lead → field report → interview → sign-off</strong> — with every spoken line sized to Sora's 4/8/12-second clip limits.</li>
<li><strong>Anchor, Reporter & Interviewee</strong>: Beyond the studio anchor, the segment features an on-location <strong>correspondent</strong> and an <strong>interviewee</strong> (an official, expert, or citizen), each rendered as their own on-camera speaker.</li>
<li><strong>Native Speech & B-Roll</strong>: Sora 2 generates synchronized audio and dialogue directly, so each speaker actually talks. The producer interleaves face-free b-roll cutaways (cityscapes, factories, solar farms, maps) to illustrate the report.</li>
<li><strong>Scene Consistency (via remix)</strong>: Sora 2 has no seed and rejects human faces in <code>input_reference</code>, so each speaker's <em>first</em> clip is a fresh generation and every later clip of that same speaker is a <strong>remix</strong> of it — reusing the source's layout, wardrobe, and lighting so the anchor/reporter/interviewee stay recognizable. Face-free b-roll is additionally chained via last-frame→first-frame (<code>input_reference</code>).</li>
<li><strong>Seamless Stitching</strong>: All clips are merged with a bundled static <code>ffmpeg</code> (via <code>imageio-ffmpeg</code>, no system package required) into a single MP4 stored in Azure Blob Storage and streamed back to the TV.</li>
<li><strong>Non-Blocking Generation</strong>: Both the decision text (topic + web research + write) and the video/narration run in background threads guarded by single-flight table locks, so the page never hangs. While today's bulletin is still being prepared the TV shows <strong>no-signal static</strong> ("Tuning in…") and re-polls <code>/get-string</code> until the text is ready; it then switches to video automatically once the segment is ready. Status is polled via <code>/genbox-video-status</code> and cached per day.</li>
<li><strong>CRT Controls, Now for Video</strong>: The <strong>lowest knob</strong> toggles between the classic scrolling text and the news video. The back/next knobs move through the timeline (loading each day's video when available), and the pause knob pauses/plays the clip. Older, text-only decisions keep working exactly as before.</li>
</ul>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h4 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Configuration</h4><a id="user-content-configuration" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Configuration" href="#configuration"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Video is generated for new dates only (configurable cutoff). Point GenBox at a dedicated Sora 2 deployment and storage container via <code>.env</code>:</p>
<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT_SORA       # Sora 2 resource endpoint(s)
AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY_SORA        # matching API key(s)
AZURE_OPENAI_MODEL_SORA=sora-2   # deployment name(s)
AZURE_OPENAI_API_VERSION_SORA=preview
AZURE_OPENAI_MODEL_TTS=tts       # text-to-speech deployment on the SAME resources
genbox_video_blob_name=genbox-video   # blob container for merged MP4s + narration
GENBOX_VIDEO_CUTOFF_DATE=2026-06-05   # only dates >= this get video + narration
GENBOX_VIDEO_ENABLED=true
GENBOX_VIDEO_MAX_CLIPS=6               # cost cap on clips per segment
GENBOX_TTS_VOICE=onyx                 # narration voice (optional)"><pre class="notranslate"><code>AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT_SORA       # Sora 2 resource endpoint(s)
AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY_SORA        # matching API key(s)
AZURE_OPENAI_MODEL_SORA=sora-2   # deployment name(s)
AZURE_OPENAI_API_VERSION_SORA=preview
AZURE_OPENAI_MODEL_TTS=tts       # text-to-speech deployment on the SAME resources
genbox_video_blob_name=genbox-video   # blob container for merged MP4s + narration
GENBOX_VIDEO_CUTOFF_DATE=2026-06-05   # only dates >= this get video + narration
GENBOX_VIDEO_ENABLED=true
GENBOX_VIDEO_MAX_CLIPS=6               # cost cap on clips per segment
GENBOX_TTS_VOICE=onyx                 # narration voice (optional)

<p dir="auto">When <code>AZURE_OPENAI_MODEL_TTS</code> is set, GenBox also narrates the daily decision in a government-spokesperson tone (via the same resources' TTS deployment). The narration renders quickly — well before the video — and plays over the scrolling text, with the scroll slowed to match the speech length. It's gated, cached, stored (in the video blob container), and referenced in the table just like the video, and served same-origin via <code>/genbox-audio</code>.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Multiple Sora resources / distributed credits.</strong> Sora's API is job-scoped: a <code>create</code> call returns a video id that only exists on the resource that served it, so the follow-up <code>poll {id}</code> and <code>download {id}</code> must hit that <em>same</em> resource — a round-robin gateway in front of several resources breaks this affinity. To spread load across resources instead, list them <strong>directly</strong> (not behind a balancer) as comma-separated values aligned by index; GenBox round-robins at the <em>job</em> level and pins each clip's whole create→poll→download lifecycle to the resource it picked (and fails a clip over to the next resource on error):</p>
<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT_SORA=https://res1.openai.azure.com,https://res2.openai.azure.com,https://res3.openai.azure.com
AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY_SORA=key1,key2,key3
AZURE_OPENAI_MODEL_SORA=sora-2   # single value applies to all, or give one per resource"><pre class="notranslate"><code>AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT_SORA=https://res1.openai.azure.com,https://res2.openai.azure.com,https://res3.openai.azure.com
AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY_SORA=key1,key2,key3
AZURE_OPENAI_MODEL_SORA=sora-2   # single value applies to all, or give one per resource
</code></pre></div>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h4 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Tech Stack</h4><a id="user-content-tech-stack-1" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Tech Stack" href="#tech-stack-1"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>OpenAI Agents SDK</strong> (<code>openai-agents</code>) — the Producer agent that scripts the segment</li>
<li><strong>Sora 2 on Azure OpenAI</strong> — text/image-to-video with native audio (<code>/openai/v1/videos</code>)</li>
<li><strong>imageio-ffmpeg</strong> — bundled static <code>ffmpeg</code> for last-frame extraction and clip concatenation</li>
<li><strong>Azure Table & Blob Storage</strong> — per-date video status/metadata and merged MP4 hosting</li>
</ul>
